title: QBF with any number of blocks
description: A quantified Boolean formula in conjunctive normal form with depth alternating blocks (exists first). One solver family S[1..depth], one link family G, and a recursive procedure refute: level i answers a candidate of level i - 1 with a clause, or with none when the candidate stands.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text: % The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.

fragments.name: level
fragments.text:
% Level i (the constant level, set per member of the family) chooses its own block.
{ val(V) } :- var(V,level).
#show val/1.

fragments.name: inner
fragments.text:
% The innermost level (level = depth) decides the formula; the other levels only choose.
last :- level = depth.
odd  :- depth \ 2 = 1.
true(C) :- lit(C,V,1), val(V).
true(C) :- lit(C,V,0), not val(V).
% An existential innermost block must satisfy every clause ...
:- last, odd, clause(C), not true(C).
own(C) :- lit(C,V,1), val(V), var(V,level).
own(C) :- lit(C,V,0), not val(V), var(V,level).
relevant(val(V)) :- last, odd, clause(C), not own(C), lit(C,V,1), val(V), var(V,B), B < level.
relevant(val(V)) :- last, odd, clause(C), not own(C), lit(C,V,0), not val(V), var(V,B), B < level.
% ... a universal one must falsify one clause.
1 { bad(C) : clause(C) } 1 :- last, not odd.
:- bad(C), true(C).
relevant(val(V)) :- bad(C), lit(C,V,_), var(V,B), B < level.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% Level i passes on the values of every block up to its own.
glue(val(V)) :- var(V,B), B <= level.

loop.text:
solver S[i in 1..depth] = shared + level + inner
link   G[i in 1..depth-1] = S[i] -> S[i+1] via shared + glue

# refute(i, M): a clause that removes the candidate M of level i - 1, or none if M stands.
# Level i looks for an answer Y. At the innermost level an answer refutes M by its relevant
# atoms. Otherwise level i + 1 tries to refute Y: if it cannot, Y refutes M, and the reason
# has two parts, what made Y legal and what made level i + 1 fail (its core, on the atoms of
# level i - 1). If it can, level i learns the clause (it names outer atoms too, so it stays
# valid) and looks again.
def refute(i, M):
    loop:
        Y = S[i].solve(assume G[i-1](M))
        if not Y: return none
        if i == S.size: return G[i-1].clause(Y)
        c = refute(i + 1, Y)
        if not c: return G[i-1].clause(Y) + S[i+1].core.on(G[i-1])
        S[i].add(c)

loop:
    M = S[1].solve()
    if not M: stop
    c = refute(2, M)
    if c: S[1].add(c)
    else:
        accept M
        S[1].add(G[1].block(M))

generators.name: qbf-blocks
generators.description: A random QBF in CNF: b alternating blocks of v variables (exists first), c clauses of three literals. Give the instance the constant depth = b.
generators.text:
% qbf-blocks: a QBF in CNF with b alternating blocks of v variables each (block 1 exists) and
% c clauses of three literals; each literal picks a variable uniformly and a sign with probability 1/2.
% Set the constant depth of the instance to b.
var(V,(V-1)/v+1) :- V = 1..b*v.
clause(1..c).
slot(1..3).
lit(C,@int(1, b*v, C, J),@flip(500, C, J, sign)) :- clause(C), slot(J).
#show var/2.
#show clause/1.
#show lit/3.

loop.text:
solver S[i in 1..depth] = shared + level + inner
link   G[i in 1..depth-1] = S[i] -> S[i+1] via shared + glue

# Block-only baseline: every answer blocks the candidate it refutes.
# refute(i, M): a clause that removes the candidate M of level i - 1, or none if M stands.
# Level i looks for an answer Y. At the innermost level an answer refutes M by its relevant
# atoms. Otherwise level i + 1 tries to refute Y: if it cannot, Y refutes M, and the reason
# has two parts, what made Y legal and what made level i + 1 fail (its core, on the atoms of
# level i - 1). If it can, level i learns the clause (it names outer atoms too, so it stays
# valid) and looks again.
def refute(i, M):
    loop:
        Y = S[i].solve(assume G[i-1](M))
        if not Y: return none
        if i == S.size: return G[i-1].block(M)
        c = refute(i + 1, Y)
        if not c: return G[i-1].block(M)
        S[i].add(c)

loop:
    M = S[1].solve()
    if not M: stop
    c = refute(2, M)
    if c: S[1].add(c)
    else:
        accept M
        S[1].add(G[1].block(M))

solver S[i in 1..depth] = shared + level + inner
link   G[i in 1..depth-1] = S[i] -> S[i+1] via shared + glue

# refute(i, M): a clause that removes the candidate M of level i - 1, or none if M stands.
# Level i looks for an answer Y. At the innermost level an answer refutes M by its relevant
# atoms. Otherwise level i + 1 tries to refute Y: if it cannot, Y refutes M, and the reason
# has two parts, what made Y legal and what made level i + 1 fail (its core, on the atoms of
# level i - 1). If it can, level i learns the clause (it names outer atoms too, so it stays
# valid) and looks again.
def refute(i, M):
    loop:
        Y = S[i].solve(assume G[i-1](M))
        if not Y: return none
        if i == S.size: return G[i-1].clause(Y)
        c = refute(i + 1, Y)
        if not c: return G[i-1].clause(Y) + S[i+1].core.on(G[i-1])
        S[i].add(c)

search S[1]:
    on candidate M:
        c = refute(2, M)
        if c: reject M with c

library.summary: A QBF with any number of quantifier blocks: a solver family, a link family and a recursive procedure (def refute) answer each level (depth = 3 here).
